attribution.note: Marcus wrote this parenthetical in his own Substack post. It is his own claim, not a quotation of anyone else.

semantics.note: The draft correctly isolates the present-tense parenthetical: generative AI had not made a net profit and was still speculative. It leaves out the separate forecast that any advantage will be minimal and short-lasting. Classing it as an observation is correct.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: no aggregate net profit for the field, cumulative through the post date, without requiring every provider to be unprofitable. The result depends on choosing industry-wide over per-provider scope, because one provider (Midjourney) claimed to be profitable.

evidence.note: Reporting on OpenAI's audited 2024 net loss of about $5B, available June 2026, before the cutoff. It covers one company only and cannot establish the industry aggregate.
Anthropic's S-1, dated before the cutoff, shows net losses every year, including $8.3B for 2024. This is a company disclosure about one firm and does not establish the industry-wide result.
In 2022, Midjourney's founder said the company was profitable, without giving a net-income figure. This counts against a universal reading but does not show the industry as a whole was profitable.

reviews.rationale: The evidence shows large losses at two leading providers, and one founder said Midjourney was profitable. None of it is an industry-wide or cumulative account of generative AI net income through May 14, 2025. The contract says losses at selected leading companies are not enough, and Midjourney's claim does not show aggregate profitability. The packet therefore cannot settle whether the field as a whole had made a net profit.
